title: Rabbi Elazar ben Antigenos
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (A Palestinian Amora of the second generation.) He was the student of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai and Hyman says he always spoke in his name, as in [Gittin 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.31a.4): “Which twenty-four-hour period? Rabbi Yochanan said: the twenty-four-hour period of examination; Rabbi Elazar ben Antigenos says in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai: the twenty-four-hour period of setting aside.” In [Chullin 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.9a.7) he speaks in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai; likewise [Chullin 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.55b.17), where Rabbah bar bar Chana disagrees with Rabbi Elazar ben Antigenos, who spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai; and at [Chullin 56b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.56b.8), he speaks in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai: “Both this and that require examination.” In [Beitzah 34a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.34a.2) the statement reads the reverse, that Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai speaks in his name; Hyman proposes the reading in Chullin, and so it is in Dikdukei Soferim. Hyman considers the same error present in [Rashi on Beitzah](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Beitzah.34a.2.5) and interprets Rashi as intending to correct it, so that one would not err in saying that he is a Tanna; therefore he says “so we read: Rabbi Elazar said,” etc., and Hyman says this resolves the difficulty raised by [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=536&lang=en). Hyman cites Shabbat 103b for his transmission in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. Hyman prefers Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai, citing the Rif and Dikdukei Soferim.[^4] Likewise we find many times in the Jerusalem Talmud that he spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai, as in [Yerushalmi Berakhot 2:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.2.6.2); Maaserot 4:3; [Yerushalmi Gittin 3:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Gittin.3.8.2); and [Yerushalmi Bava Metzia 7:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Metzia.7.4.2). In [Yerushalmi Berakhot 5:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.5.2.14), “Rabbi Ze’ira, Rabbi Elazar ben Antigenos in the name of Rabbi Yannai”; Hyman proposes Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai.[^3]

notes.text: מע״ל is מעת לעת, a twenty-four-hour period, not an unexplained maal. Saved Davidson Gittin31a fully writes Elazar ben Antigenos and Elazar son of Yannai, supporting these connected expansions. The inspection/setting-aside alternatives remain without an invented forward/backward direction. All teacher reversals, Rashi interpretations and Eliezer ben Yaakov substitutions remain Hyman’s conjectures; בקד״ס is read as בדק״ס.

Gittin 31a ends after the named transmission;31b begins with the twenty-four-hour period of setting aside. The consulted Beitzah 34a and its Rashi both transmit Elazar son of Yannai in the name of Elazar ben Antigenos. Hyman’s reversal proposal and interpretation of Rashi remain his, alongside that directly consulted reading. Exact Rif and Dikdukei Soferim claims remain attributed.

The Gittin chain ends at 31a and its ruling begins at [Gittin 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.31b.1). The linked Beitzah and its Rashi both make Elazar son of Yannai transmit in Antigenos’s name. Several linked Yerushalmi passages have the other direction, and Yerushalmi Berakhot 5:2 brackets part of the name. Hyman’s proposal about Beitzah and his interpretation of Rashi remain distinct from the text of the consulted comparison.

In the havdalah discussion at [Shabbat 150b:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.150b.11), Rabbi Elazar ben Antigenos speaks in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. In the Vilna text of [Rif Shabbat 64a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Shabbat.64a.10), the speaker is Rabbi Eliezer ben Antigenos, and he cites Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai. Hyman gives Shabbat 103b. The Dikdukei Soferim variant is cited as he reports it.
